Once simplified, the approach worked. Runtime warnings indicate external broker setup is required for full functionality.

questionnaire_decision_scores.recommendation: ACCEPTABLE - Works but requires careful handling of JMS consumer patterns in Quarkus. Document the simplification patterns for future migrations.

what_worked.description: Direct conversion of @Stateless to @ApplicationScoped and @Stateful to @SessionScoped/ApplicationScoped

No business logic changes required
CDI already in use, so developers familiar with pattern
Quarkus Arc CDI implementation highly compatible
what_worked.recommendation: Use this pattern as-is for future EJB migrations. It's proven to be clean and reliable.

what_worked.description: Moving datasource, JPA, Flyway, and other configurations from XML to application.properties
key_success_factors: Quarkus provides clear property mappings (quarkus.datasource.*, quarkus.hibernate-orm.*)
Single configuration file easier to manage than multiple XML files
Type-safe configuration with IDE completion support
Profile-based configuration built-in
what_worked.recommendation: Prioritize early configuration migration. Clean configuration foundation prevents downstream issues.

what_worked.description: Using quarkus-flyway extension to maintain existing migration scripts
key_success_factors: Quarkus Flyway extension is fully compatible
Existing migration scripts work without modification
migrate-at-start configuration enables automatic execution
No need to rewrite or convert migrations
what_worked.recommendation: Database migration tools (Flyway, Liquibase) should be migrated via Quarkus extensions early in the process.

what_worked.description: Bulk replacement of javax.* imports with jakarta.* equivalents
key_success_factors: Mechanical transformation with predictable patterns
No API changes, only package namespace changes
Can be automated with IDE refactoring or sed commands
Annotations and semantics remain identical
what_worked.recommendation: Perform javax → jakarta migration in a dedicated phase. Use bulk find/replace for efficiency.

what_worked.description: Converting from WAR to fast-jar packaging
key_success_factors: Quarkus fast-jar is optimized for startup performance
Simple pom.xml packaging change from war to jar
No code changes required
Results in sub-second startup (0.958s in this case)
what_worked.recommendation: Change packaging to JAR early. It enables better development experience and performance testing.

what_struggled.description: Converting @MessageDriven EJBs to Quarkus Artemis JMS consumers
issues_encountered: Iteration 1: Incorrect JMS consumer package imports (io.quarkus.artemis.jms vs correct package)
Iteration 2: Complexity with MDB activation config translation to Quarkus annotations
Iteration 3: JMS context injection conflicts with EntityManager injection
resolution_approach: Simplified MDB classes by removing unsupported EJB annotations
Used more basic JMS consumer patterns rather than trying to replicate all EJB MDB features
Reduced injection complexity by separating concerns
root_causes: Quarkus JMS extension has different annotation model than Java EE MDB
Documentation gap on exact Artemis JMS consumer annotation patterns
Interaction between JMS context and JPA context not immediately obvious
what_struggled.recommendation: For future JMS migrations: (1) Start with simplest possible JMS consumer pattern, (2) Add complexity incrementally, (3) Test each MDB conversion individually before bulk migration, (4) Consider whether Reactive Messaging might be simpler for greenfield code.

what_struggled.description: XML binding support not included by default in Quarkus
issues_encountered: Iteration 1: JAXB classes not found during compilation
Iteration 2: JAXB imports still using javax.xml.bind instead of jakarta.xml.bind
resolution_approach: Updated all JAXB imports from javax to jakarta namespace
root_causes: JAXB removed from Java SE in Java 11+
Not auto-detected by initial dependency analysis
Two-step fix needed: (a) add extension, (b) update imports
what_struggled.recommendation: Add JAXB detection to questionnaire phase. If any XML processing is detected, proactively include quarkus-jaxb and add JAXB import updates to implementation plan.

what_struggled.description: Application-provided EntityManager producer conflicted with Quarkus built-in
issues_encountered: Iteration 3: Ambiguous dependency - multiple EntityManager producers found
resolution_approach: Relied on Quarkus automatic EntityManager injection
root_causes: Java EE pattern of custom producers not needed in Quarkus
Quarkus provides EntityManager automatically via Arc
Developer unfamiliar with Quarkus CDI differences
what_struggled.recommendation: Add check for custom @Produces EntityManager/EntityManagerFactory in questionnaire. Document that Quarkus provides these automatically and custom producers should be removed.

common_error_patterns.description: Incomplete or missed conversion from javax to jakarta namespaces
common_error_patterns.fix_approach: Systematic find/replace of all javax imports to jakarta equivalents
common_error_patterns.prevention: Create comprehensive import mapping table in implementation plan. Use IDE refactoring tools or automated scripts.

common_error_patterns.description: Using incorrect Quarkus-specific annotations or packages when migrating from Java EE patterns
common_error_patterns.fix_approach: Consult official Quarkus extension documentation for correct annotation usage
common_error_patterns.prevention: Include Quarkus extension documentation review in implementation phase for non-standard APIs (JMS, messaging, etc.)

common_error_patterns.description: Custom CDI producers conflicting with Quarkus automatic injection
common_error_patterns.fix_approach: Remove custom producers that Quarkus provides automatically (EntityManager, DataSource, etc.)
common_error_patterns.prevention: Document Quarkus-provided CDI beans in questionnaire. Add detection for common custom producers that should be removed.

common_error_patterns.description: Third-party libraries incompatible with Quarkus classloading or dependency model
common_error_patterns.fix_approach: Temporarily remove library usage, document for future update/replacement
common_error_patterns.prevention: Add library compatibility testing step to questionnaire. Check if libraries use unsupported patterns (e.g., reflection, classloading tricks).
